site.name: pelagic
site.summary: pelagic-clone Marketing site (landing page) for the fictional open-source vector database Pelagic. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page landing: top nav + animated GitHub-stars counter pill; hero with title, dual CTAs, `pip install` copy strip, rotating benchmark numbers, right-side 4-language (Python / Node / Go / curl) code tabs; Trusted-by logo row; 3 core-feature cards; Ingest → Index → Query three-step flow; architecture SVG diagram; customer quote cards; left Blog 5 posts + right Changelog 5 entries dual feed; 4-column footer with sitemap | | `styles.css` | Brand color #0E5C8A deep-sea blue; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 3 breakpoints (>1100 / 880–1100 / <880) | | `script.js` | Stars-counter 1.2s eased animation; code tabs switch Python / Node / Go / curl; benchmark rows rotate every 2.5s; `pip install pelagic` copy toast; fictional-logo rendering |

run_plan.goal: Validate the UX of the Pelagic single-page landing site, focusing on developer onboarding flows (code snippets, install commands), content hierarchy, and mobile responsiveness.
run_plan.summary: The run will treat index.html as a comprehensive single-page application. It begins by verifying the hero section's value proposition and interactive code tabs. It then proceeds to validate the 'How it fits' workflow and architecture diagrams. Finally, it assesses the footer navigation and repeats critical checks on mobile viewports to address known tap-target risks.
assumptions: Navigation links (Product, Docs, Pricing) are in-page anchors (#id) rather than external pages, given the single HTML file structure.
The 'Copy' button triggers a visual toast notification or state change defined in script.js.
Code tabs switch content dynamically without page reloads.
risk_hotspots: Mobile Navigation: High density of small tap targets (<44px) in the header.
Code Tabs: Ensuring Python/Node/Go/curl switches update content correctly.
Install Command: Verifying the 'Copy' interaction provides clear user feedback.
Benchmark Animation: Checking if rotating numbers cause layout shifts or distraction.

phases.title: Hero & Developer Onboarding
phases.objective: Validate the primary conversion path: understanding the product and getting started via code/install.
key_checks: Click all 4 code tabs (Python, Node, Go, curl) to verify content switching.
Click 'Copy' on the pip install strip to verify toast/feedback.
Verify 'Quickstart' and 'View on GitHub' buttons are clickable and distinct.
Check legibility of the animated benchmark text.

phases.title: Feature Deep-Dive & Architecture
phases.objective: Ensure technical claims (Hybrid search, FAISS drop-in) and architectural diagrams are readable and logically ordered.
key_checks: Scroll to 'Built for the way modern retrieval actually works' section.
Verify readability of the 3 core feature cards.
Inspect the 'Ingest → Index → Query' flow diagram for clarity.
Check the Architecture SVG for scaling issues or missing labels.
exit_criteria: Logical flow of the 3-step process is visually clear.

phases.title: Social Proof & Footer Navigation
phases.objective: Validate trust signals and ensure all footer links resolve to valid in-page anchors or external resources.
key_checks: Scan 'Trusted by' logo row for rendering issues.
Review Blog and Changelog feeds for date/content formatting.
Click through footer sitemap links (Overview, Hybrid search, Managed, etc.).
Verify external community links (GitHub, Discord, Forum).
exit_criteria: Footer links navigate to correct sections or open new tabs appropriately.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility
phases.objective: Stress-test the layout on mobile viewports, specifically addressing the prescan warnings about small tap targets.
key_checks: Test hamburger menu (if present) or stacked nav accessibility.
Attempt to tap header links (Product, Docs, Pricing) to check for overlap/mis-clicks.
Verify code block horizontal scrolling behavior on small screens.
Check font sizes for readability on mobile.
exit_criteria: Nav items are distinguishable and tappable.
Code blocks are usable (scrollable or wrapped).
No critical content is hidden or overlapping.

coverage_targets.pages: 100% of index.html sections (Hero, Features, Architecture, Social, Footer)
coverage_targets.features: All 4 code tabs, Copy button, All nav links, All footer links
coverage_targets.mobile: Full pass on mobile viewport with focus on header and code blocks

notes: Since this is a single-page site, 'navigation' testing primarily involves checking smooth scrolling to anchors.
Pay close attention to the 'script.js' interactions: if the stars counter or benchmark rotator causes jank, note it.
The prescan identified multiple 'small_tap_target' warnings; Phase 4 is critical for validating if these are actual usability blockers.

Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 17.9k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl import { Pelagic } from "pelagic"; const db = new Pelagic({ apiKey: "pk_live_…" }); const index = await db.createIndex({ name: "docs", dim: 1536, metric: "cosine", hybrid: true, }); await index.upsert([ { id: "doc-001", vector: await embed(text), filter: { lang: "en" } }, ]); const hits = await index.query({ vector: await embed("what is hnsw"), topK: 10, filter: { lang: "en" }, rerank: "bge-large", }); 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop."
